thread:
alin: Quick follow-up on the metadata RFC — we've hit repeated ambiguity around 'lease' vs 'scope' when clients resolve a model during a rollout. Can we align on a minimal schema that prevents split-brain and supports safe fallback?

maya: +1. Main pain is tenants pinning a model while infra wants to allow autoscale fallback variants. We need explicit fields for 'lease_hardness' and an ordered 'allowed_fallbacks'.

tom: Also: handoff semantics. When a canary completes and becomes global, how do we atomically transfer 'ownership' without clients reading a half-updated manifest?

jordan: One naive option was a big 'delimitation' blob with start/end and safety_set, but that feels heavy to parse in the hot-path resolver.

sophia: Could we do compact primitives instead? e.g. `lease_type`: `hard|soft|grace`, plus `grace_seconds` and `fallback_priority` (list). Fast to eval, small footprint.

alin: Sketching a compact example we could standardize on (pseudo-JSON snippet):

```json
{
  "model_ref": "hf:acme/assistant@v2",
  "lease_type": "soft-with-grace",
  "grace_seconds": 900,
  "owner": "tenant:acme",
  "safety_set": ["v2-fp16", "v2-quant"],
  "allowed_fallbacks": ["v1", "v2-small"],
  "hand_off_probe": "canary-ok:95pct-latency",
  "annotation": "canary->global handoff window"
}
```

maya: Love that. A couple clarifications: 1) `safety_set` is advisory — runtime can still pick best perf candidate within it; 2) `allowed_fallbacks` must be ordered to convey priority.

tom: We should define resolver semantics precisely: read manifest -> if `lease_type==hard` then treat owner as mandatory (no fallback unless owner explicit), if `soft` then fallbacks allowed immediately, if `soft-with-grace` then allow fallbacks only after `grace_seconds` expire or health probe fails.

jordan: For atomic handoff: add `hand_off_token` (monotonic string) that the rollout system rotates when it intends to change owner. Clients accept only manifests with an increasing token to avoid partial reads during writes.

sophia: That helps. But tokens require quorum writes on the control plane. We should note performance/consistency tradeoffs in the RFC.

opsbot: deploy-bot: updated rollout-manifest schema v2 deployed to staging at 2026-03-21T15:42Z :rocket:

maya: Telemetry: emit `lease.resolve` events with fields {manifest_token, lease_type, resolved_model, fallback_used?}. We'll need this to debug customer cases where they expected an owner pin but saw a fallback.

alin: Ops constraints: runtime resolver must remain sub-ms when cached. So the canonical manifest needs to be compact and cache-friendly; heavy evaluation (health-probe checks, token rotations) should be offloaded to the rollout service which periodically annotates the manifest.

sophia: On migration: backfill existing pins into new compact fields off-line, but keep backward-compatibility in the resolver for one release. Add a compatibility shim that translates legacy `pin_affinity` -> `lease_type` + `allowed_fallbacks`.

jordan: Tests: unit for resolver combinatorics (hard vs soft vs grace), integration that simulates partial writes with `hand_off_token` rotations, and an e2e perf test to make sure cache hit path stays <1ms p95.

tom: Ops action: add a flag to dedicated clusters to enforce `hard` leases for enterprise tenants if requested. That prevents accidental fallback to cheaper variants for SLO-critical customers.

maya: Noted. Also propose a short-lived annotation `migration_hint` so rollout tools can stage canaries without changing core semantics. Example: `migration_hint: "staging-only"`.

alin: Action items I see: 1) finalize minimal schema fields (lease_type, grace_seconds, owner, safety_set, allowed_fallbacks, hand_off_token), 2) write resolver semantics doc + state machine, 3) add telemetry events, 4) implement compatibility shim and backfill plan, 5) add tests & perf gating.

sophia: I'll draft the resolver semantics doc. @maya can you lead the telemetry schema? @tom can you sketch the `hand_off_token` rotation implementation?

maya: Yep, will draft telemetry and include sample datadog keys.

tom: On it; will put a prototype PR for `hand_off_token` in the rollout service.

jordan: I'll start the unit test matrix and performance harness changes.

alin: Thanks everyone — let's aim to land the RFC update + shim in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
